jobs.title: Write a handler, an adapter or an extension file
jobs.description: Every name a step handler, a service adapter, a processor or an extension file uses from @sensigo/realm, each with its declaration.
jobs.purpose: A step's own work runs in a step handler (`StepHandler`), a call to an outside service in a service adapter (`ServiceAdapter`), and a project's extension file exports them for `realm.yaml` to name. This page lists the interfaces such code implements, the helper functions it can call, the error it throws (`WorkflowError`), and every type their declarations refer to that no other page holds first.

jobs.title: Define and load a workflow
jobs.description: The loaders that read a workflow into a WorkflowDefinition, and the types of the definition they return.
jobs.purpose: `loadWorkflowFromFile` and `loadWorkflowFromString` read a workflow and return its `WorkflowDefinition`; their `…WithDiagnostics` forms also return the loader's warnings and the paths it could not check. This page lists the loaders, the error codes Realm raises, and the definition's types; what each field of the workflow file means is on the workflow reference pages.

handPages.title: Core library: run a workflow from your own program

jobs.title: Run and drive a run from a program
jobs.description: The functions a program calls to step, advance, answer and abandon runs, with the option and reply types they use.
jobs.purpose: A program that drives runs itself calls these functions with a `RunStore` and a `WorkflowDefinition`: `executeStep`, `executeChain` and `advanceRun` move a run forward, `submitHumanResponse` answers an open question, and `abandonRun` ends a run. Each returns an `EngineReply`, except `abandonRun`, which returns the run's `RunRecord`. This page lists them, the other functions the docs name for driving runs, and every type they reach that no more specific page holds.

handPages.title: Core library: run a workflow from your own program

jobs.title: Implement a store
jobs.description: The store interfaces a program implements to keep runs in a store of its own, the stores Realm ships, and the helpers a store calls.
jobs.purpose: A `RunStore` keeps runs; the other store interfaces keep what Realm stores beside them, such as refused answers (`FailedAttemptStore`), trace lines (`TraceBufferStore`) and registered workflows (`WorkflowRegistrar`). This page lists those interfaces, the stores Realm ships that implement them, and the helpers a store calls for its clock, its readings and its settlements.

handPages.title: Core library: the run store interface

jobs.title: Embed the MCP server
jobs.description: The functions that serve Realm's MCP tools from a program of your own, their options, and the types those options name.
jobs.purpose: `createRealmMcpServer` (from `@sensigo/realm-mcp`) takes a run store and a workflow store in its options and returns an MCP server; `createRealmMcpServerOnHome` (from `@sensigo/realm-mcp/home`) opens a Realm home and returns the server with a `close` function. This page lists both, their options, and the types those options name that no other page holds first. The `failureText` option is `shown`, the default, or `hidden`, which shows an assistant in `get_run_state` the length of a failure's words in place of the words; `REALM_MCP_FAILURE_TEXT` also sets it, and `hidden` wins. See [Failure text](../mcp/run-state-and-health.md#failure-text).

handPages.title: Core library: serve MCP from your own program

jobs.title: Read a run's record or export from a program
jobs.description: The run record's types, the evidence entry's, and the functions that read a run's phase and an entry's sources.
jobs.purpose: A run's record (`RunRecord`) is one object that holds everything Realm knows about the run, and `realm run export` writes all of it into a bundle. `deriveRunPhase` gives a run's phase from its record, and `outputSourceOf` and `readSupplier` say where an evidence entry's output and supplier came from. A record written before Realm recorded how a run ended has no `sealed_by`: `classifyLegacySeal` gives the arm it would have carried, and `armToOutcome` the outcome an arm means. This page lists the record's types, the evidence entry's, and those functions.
